title: The Memorare
hookLine: remember, O most gracious Virgin, that never was it known

cards: Never. Asking for something usually comes wrapped in hedges. Sorry to bother you.
No pressure. Only if you have time. Here's a prayer that does the opposite.
It doesn't open by asking; it opens by reminding.
Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, it begins, that never was it known that anyone who fled to your protection, asked for your help, or sought your prayers, was left without help.

teach.b: Memorare is Latin for remember, and it names the prayer. The one praying asks Mary to remember her own record, the way you'd speak to a friend who has always come through: you know what you're like.

teach.h: NEVER WAS IT KNOWN: A STATEMENT OF TRUST.
teach.b: Then the bold line, never was it known. It isn't a survey or a statistic. It's a statement of trust, the kind people make about those they love: in the stories handed down, she didn't turn anyone away.
Where does that trust come from? Some Catholics point to a wedding at Cana. In John's Gospel, the wine runs out, and Mary notices and tells her son.
In the Douay-Rheims: "They have no wine." Then she turns to the servants: "Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye." She sees a need and brings it to Jesus.
The Memorare asks her to do that again. Then the posture.
Inspired with this confidence, it goes on, I fly to you, and before you I stand, sinful and sorrowful. Confidence and humility in one breath: I know you'll help, and I know I don't deserve it.
It ends by asking the mother of the Word made flesh not to despise these words, but to hear and answer.

teach.h: WHATSOEVER HE SHALL SAY TO YOU, DO YE.
teach.b: Who wrote it? Tradition credits Saint Bernard of Clairvaux, and others trace its spread to a later French priest, also named Bernard. Nobody needs to settle that to pray it.
The prayer itself only asks you to remember.

how: Catholics pray the Memorare on their own, in hard moments and as a regular devotion, and some pray it in a short run of repetitions when they bring an urgent need to Mary.

games.q: you're a guest at a wedding in Cana, and you notice the wine has run out. what do you do?
o: say nothing. it's not your party.
go to Jesus: they have no wine.
slip out before it gets awkward.
games.why: Mary goes to her son with "they have no wine," then tells the servants, "whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye" (John 2:3–5). the Memorare asks her to notice again.

practice: Bring one need to mind, the one you'd hedge about if you were asking a person, and name it plainly, without the sorry-to-bother-you.
If you pray, pray the Memorare once, slowly, from remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, to hear and answer me, and set your need inside it like a note in an envelope.
If you don't, remember one time someone noticed what you needed before you asked, and came.
